newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to push for free trade before Chile summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to push for free trade before Chile summit.

text.p: The Clinton administration hopes to make progress expanding hemispheric free trade by the time officials from the Americas begin next year summit in Santiago, Chile, a U.S. official said Thursday.

White House Special Envoy to the Americas Thomas McClarty said the U.S. government was seeking "fast track" legislation from Congress to negotiate Chile's inclusion to the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) between the U.S., Mexico and Canada.
"We hope and believe we can make significant progress on the trade agenda by the Santiago summit," he said at a conference of Latin American and U.S. business figures sponsored by Smith Barney.
He also said that plans for a Free Trade Agreement of the Americas, set out at the 1994 Summit of the Americas, were on track to be implemented by the declared goal of 2005.
"Building the Free Trade Area of the Americas with a specific timeline must be a high priority," McClarty said.
President Clinton, who visited Mexico and Central America in May, will travel to South America later this year, before attending the hemispheric summit to Santiago in 1998, McClarty said.
"This is an ambitious and even an historic schedule of presidential commitment and engagement," McClarty said. "It shows our continued commitment to the hemisphere at the very highest level."
